cases.id: case:P: a negative price is never affordable
cases.note: Group P. Player:canAfford(-100) on a stand-in with 500 must be exactly false.

Passes in the unchanged starter (starter.execution.json): with 500 in the wallet 100 is affordable and 600 is not. It is also the positive boundary of the #6218 fix (a 'refuse every purchase' fix must not pass), hence overlap.

known_issues: Report/defect mismatch in group V: the starter's isMoneyBag compares the class with GAMEMODE.Config.MoneyClass, the shipped config sets that to 'spawned_money' (environment/darkrp/gamemode/config/config.lua:328) and DarkRP.createMoneyBag creates exactly that class (gamemode/modules/money/sv_money.lua:42). On an unmodified server dropped money is therefore still recognised and report #6236 does not reproduce; it only differs for an entity that carries ENT.IsSpawnedMoney under another class. The case (benchmarks/darkrp-core/private/harbor/darkrp-door-economy-regressions/tests/suite.lua:179-190) uses a stand-in whose class is 't2b_not_the_config_class', so a fix by class name (e.g. also accepting 'spawned_money') fails; only honouring the IsSpawnedMoney flag (set in entities/entities/spawned_money/shared.lua:6 and read nowhere in the starter) passes.

Group P is asserted through Player:canAfford only (benchmarks/darkrp-core/private/harbor/darkrp-door-economy-regressions/tests/suite.lua:78-91). The report describes the balance moving the wrong way when spending and never names the predicate; a fix that rejects or clamps negative prices where items are declared or bought would stop the exploit but fail. The stand-in player exposes only getDarkRPVar and the call is not wrapped in pcall, so a canAfford that touches any other player method errors.

Group Q stand-in (benchmarks/darkrp-core/private/harbor/darkrp-door-economy-regressions/tests/suite.lua:94-103, fakeDoor at 54-67): ownership is visible only through door:getDoorOwner(); the door data table has no 'owner' field. An implementation that compares doorData.owner with ply:UserID() (equivalent in the engine, where getDoorOwner is Player(doorData.owner)) fails Q. Group R's door does carry owner = 9. Control alternative-strict-reading demonstrates this: it fails exactly Q.

Exact-boolean expectations: S requires the group-chat predicate to return exactly true/false and V requires isMoneyBag to return exactly true/false (benchmarks/darkrp-core/private/harbor/darkrp-door-economy-regressions/tests/suite.lua:138-143, 181-188), while Q, R and W coerce with 'or false'. An implementation returning a truthy non-boolean (e.g. the flag value or a table entry) would fail S or V although every caller only tests truthiness.

benchmarks/darkrp-core/private/harbor/darkrp-door-economy-regressions/tests/suite.lua declares 'local n' and 'uniq' twice (lines 14-15 and 33-34); case T builds its name from the counter without incrementing it (line 149). Harmless in one run, noted for readers.
